data.turoyo: Hiya ftəḥla u=tarʕo d u=ḥəmmam w haṯe tfišola lawġul w ela ṣxəlla u=tarʕo d u=ḥəmmam.
data.translation: machte die Tür des Bades auf, stieß es hinein und verschloß die Türe des Bades.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; human forced insertion clarifies the meaning already exemplified by stuffed bridles. Use the assigned verse only, excluding the reader's extra preceding sentence.
Clarifies an already attested insertion meaning: 29/457 stuffs bridles under a stone, while 88/250 shoves a person inside; the old obstruction-only gloss excludes both.

summary: The two original quotations are already supplied verbatim and are not added again. Their semantic contrast motivates a meaning clarification rather than a formatting rewrite.
The new tfišola has an assimilated/variant s/š surface form; retain it verbatim and provisionally file with existing tfs. No independent tfš root is established.
The established frame has an affected object plus location/goal. At 99/48 the b-marked gate occurs without an overt affected object; its interpretation remains unsettled.
At 99/48 does tfəsle bi darga describe striking/knocking at the gate, pushing against it, or blocking the entrance? Do not publish a new knock sense before confirming.
Confirm s/š in tfišola at 88/250 against tfisile; the supplied evidence supports the insertion family but does not explain the phonological variation.
Insertion takes a human patient at 88/250 as well as bridles at 29/457. The meaning is clarified in the gloss rather than split by participant type.
